Active/standby DHCP with a confirmed replica over a dedicated cable. Request DHCP on the clients and advance the simulation. OSPFv2 includes per-flow ECMP, stub/NSSA areas, summarization, conditional default route, and MD5. BGP includes prefix-lists/route-maps, peer-groups, maximum-prefix, and TCP MD5. DHCP snooping, DAI, IP source guard, port-security, voice VLAN, and root/loop guard act on forwarding. UDLD uses single-hop advertisements/echo and eight attempts before err-disable; its timing is simplified and there is no PCAP codec. Single-hop asynchronous IPv4 BFD uses UDP/3784 and brings down OSPF adjacencies; no Echo, Demand, authentication, multihop, or BGP integration. Native 802.1X drives the existing EAPOL/RADIUS model; it is not a complete implementation of all EAP methods.

ACL/interface-based PAT, NTP, timezone, virtual configuration files, ICMP IP SLA, tracking, and inventory/error/forwarding queries use the model's real state. MPLS uses manual LFIB/FEC, without LDP. Encrypted tunnels use an educational handshake, without the full IKEv2 CLI or an interoperable IKEv2/ESP format. The model's NETCONF/RESTCONF is not equivalent to native Cisco management over certified SSH/TLS.

ICMP/HTTP/Modbus accept IPv6, VRF, and link-local scope. Other scenario adapters use IPv4 in the default table. Dynamic VRF protocols not implemented.
A load can have multiple UPS units: it stays powered while a requested source has output. Each UPS reserves the full rated power; does not represent real electrical switching.

Ethernet/IP/TCP, OSPFv2/MD5, HSRPv1/v2 without authentication, BFD, CDP/LLDP, Modbus, DNS, DHCPv4/v6, syslog, VXLAN, and BGP/EVPN have binary codecs with validation. Exporting/decoding does not attest interoperability with Cisco devices. Protocols without a codec, legacy OSPF HMAC authentication, and legacy OSPF headers without metadata are explicitly excluded. The DHCP replica channel has no vendor codec.

Simplified tank, level 0–1000. PLC: 100 ms scan, holding 0=setpoint, input 0=level, coil 0=pump, discrete 0=latched alarm. HMI/SCADA read every 1 s; MES every 2 s, over binary Modbus TCP, 800 ms deadline. Pumping stops when the PLC is powered off; draining continues within the scan resolution limits. Neither the network nor the A/B power feeds replicate the PLC. No ladder logic, firmware, functional safety, or certified physics.
